instructions: Heat a grill to medium-high, or heat a grill pan over medium-high heat for 5 minutes.

Make the salmoriglio. Mince the garlic. Juice the lemons. That should be about 1/3 cup. Whisk the garlic, the lemon juice, the oregano, the oil, 1/2 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper in a bowl.
Spoon 1/4 cup of the salmoriglio into a small bowl and set it aside for the table.
Pat the chicken dry. Season it with the rest of the salt and pepper, then toss it with 2 tbsp of the salmoriglio.

Grill the chicken for 6 minutes, until it has dark grill marks and lets go of the grate. Flip and grill for 6 minutes. You're cooking it to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when there's no pink left.
Transfer the chicken to a large skillet over medium heat. Pour in the rest of the salmoriglio and turn the pieces in it for 2 minutes.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Serve the chicken with the pan sauce spooned over and the reserved salmoriglio in a bowl on the table.
method_notes: The sources agree that salmoriglio is just olive oil, lemon, garlic and oregano, whisked and spooned over grilled chicken. The lead finishes the chicken in a hot pan with most of the sauce and keeps a little back for the table, and this does the same. It uses boneless thighs so the grilling takes 12 minutes. Amounts are scaled from a whole chicken to 2 lbs of thighs.
